locator.text: Equation (B.28), p. 152, in the proof of Proposition B.5

evidence: paper: p_s - p_{s,r} = O(y e_a), \qquad E_r/E = 1 + O(y e_a).

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both clauses are stated, with the paper's O(·) written out as an explicit uniform constant. First clause: p_s = (X Q_s/L, X N_s/(L E)) by (4.11), and Lean's two stock coordinates are exactly profileStockOne = X · angularLag/L and profileStockTwo = X · axialLag/(L · E) (the docstring at ProfileHistories.lean:587 says 'The printed N_s is the regular primitive divided by X'); `log_stocks_uniform_jets` bounds the actual-minus-reference difference of both by M·y·activation T κ y = M y e_a, for every jet order n and with M independent of T (= t₁) and of κ (= κ₀) — matching the paper's 'holds for field values and parameter derivatives' and 'uniform as t₁ and κ₀ decrease'. Second clause: Lean states it in the paper's own direction, E_r/E - 1, as `inverse_relative_uniform_jets`; the rewriting is only that E = √(2X)·(angular field) on both sides (Lean's `velocity`), so the common √(2X) — and the paper's constant C in E = C^{-1}√(2X)φ — cancel from the ratio and E_r/E = referenceAngular/activatedAngular. No constant, exponent or sign differs; the Lean statement is if anything more explicit (all parameter jets, uniform constants down to κ = 0).
